'''Micah Charles Lasher''' (born December 18, 1981)<ref>{{cite web | title=Micah Lasher Voter Registration | website=New York State Voter Records | url=https://stevemorse.org/nysvoters/nysvoters.php?FirstNameKind=exact&FirstNameMax=Micah&MiddleNameKind=exact&MiddleNameMax=&LastNameKind=exact&LastNameMax=Lasher&NameSuffixKind=exact&NameSuffixMax=&HouseNumberKind=exact&HouseNumberMax=&FractionKind=exact&FractionMax=&ApartmentKind=exact&ApartmentMax=&PreStreetDirectionKind=exact&PreStreetDirectionMax=&streetKind=exact&streetMax=&PostStreetDirectionKind=exact&PostStreetDirectionMax=&CityKind=exact&CityMax=&CountyKind=exact&CountyMax=&Zip5Kind=exact&Zip5Max=&Zip4Kind=exact&Zip4Max=&MailAddress1Kind=exact&MailAddress1Max=&MailAddress2Kind=exact&MailAddress2Max=&MailAddress3Kind=exact&MailAddress3Max=&MailAddress4Kind=exact&MailAddress4Max=&DateofBirthKind=starts&DateofBirthMax=&GenderKind=exact&GenderMax=&PartyKind=exact&PartyMax=&number=a&ElectionDistrictKind=exact&ElectionDistrictMax=&LegislativeDistrictKind=exact&LegislativeDistrictMax=&TownKind=exact&TownMax=&WardKind=exact&WardMax=&CongressionalDistrictKind=exact&CongressionalDistrictMax=&SenateDistrictKind=exact&SenateDistrictMax=&AssemblyDistrictKind=exact&AssemblyDistrictMax=&LastDateVotedKind=exact&LastDateVotedMax=&LastYearVotedKind=exact&LastYearVotedMax=&LastCountyVotedKind=exact&LastCountyVotedMax=&LastRegisteredAddressKind=exact&LastRegisteredAddressMax=&LastRegisteredNameKind=exact&LastRegisteredNameMax=&AssignedCountyKind=exact&AssignedCountyMax=&DateApplicationReceivedKind=exact&DateApplicationReceivedMax=&ApplicationSourceKind=exact&ApplicationSourceMax=&IDRequiredKind=exact&IDRequiredMax=&IDVerifiedKind=exact&IDVerifiedMax=&VoterStatusKind=exact&VoterStatusMax=&StatusReasonKind=exact&StatusReasonMax=&DateInactiveKind=exact&DateInactiveMax=&DatePurgedKind=exact&DatePurgedMax=&IDKind=exact&IDMax=&VoterHistoryKind=exact&VoterHistoryMax=&offset=1&pagesize=50}}</ref> is an American politician who is the U.S. Representative-elect for [[New York's 12th congressional district|New York's 12th Congressional District]].<ref name="ReynoldsSmithRennisonBlum2026-1">{{Cite news |last=Reynolds |first=Evan |last2=Smith |first2=Mitch |last3=Rennison |first3=Joe |last4=Blum |first4=Dani |last5=Yoon |first5=John |last6=Igielnik |first6=Ruth |last7=Cave |first7=Damien |last8=Klavens |first8=Alex |last9=Harmon |first9=Amy |date=2026-11-03 |title=New York 12th Congressional District 2026: Live Election Results, Lasher vs. Shinkle |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/11/03/us/elections/results-new-york-us-house-12.html |access-date=2026-11-04 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> 

Lasher has served as a member of the [[New York State Assembly]] for [[New York's 69th State Assembly district|District 69]] in [[Manhattan]] in New York City since 2025, a position he will maintain until his term ends on January 1, 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Endorsements by Micah Lasher |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Endorsements_by_Micah_Lasher |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref> He will be sworn into Congress when the new session begins on January 3, 2027.<ref name="www.congress.gov-1" />

He was previously the Director of State Legislative Affairs under [[New York City Mayor]] [[Michael Bloomberg]], the Chief of Staff of [[NY State Attorney General]] [[Eric Schneiderman]], and the Director of Policy for [[New York Governor]] [[Kathy Hochul]].

== Early life and education ==
He was born in [[Manhattan]] to Stephanie Lasher and Albert C. Lasher.<ref name=marry/><ref name=rod>[https://patch.com/new-york/upper-west-side-nyc/election-q-meet-ny-12-candidate-micah-lasher "Election Q&A: Meet NY-12 Candidate Micah Lasher,"] Patch, June 12, 2026.</ref>  Lasher grew up on the [[Upper West Side]] of Manhattan.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last1=Kumar |first1=Arundhati |last2=Blum |first2=Gillian |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Lasher Wins 69th District Assembly Primary, Northrup Runner Up in Five-Way Race |url=https://www.westsidespirit.com/news/lasher-wins-69th-district-assembly-primary-northrup-runner-up-in-five-way-race-JB3461478 |access-date=2024-11-24 |website=West Side Spirit |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Saltonstall |first=Gus |date=2024-05-30 |title=A WSR Conversation With Candidate Micah Lasher in the Run-Up to the UWS, Morningside Heights Assembly Election |url=https://www.westsiderag.com/2024/05/30/a-conversation-with-candidate-micah-lasher-in-the-lead-up-to-the-uws-morningside-heights-assembly-election |access-date=2024-11-24 |website=West Side Rag |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1994/06/13/us/as-life-s-questions-get-harder-magic-casts-a-wider-spell.html?searchResultPosition=1 "As Life's Questions Get Harder, Magic Casts a Wider Spell,"] The New York Times, June 13, 1994.</ref>

Lasher performed [[Magic (illusion)|magic]] tricks on national television by the age of 13, appearing on the  ''[[Late Show with David Letterman]]'' and on NBC's ''[[Today (American TV program)|Today]]'' show.<ref name=yahoo>[https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/tradition-reigns-one-richest-congressional-180000388.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAGZ0hRDNLe-KHM1PnwKSH3KlzpHsYHkGYGar64nFg8f-S50P0EahO0DrbecrC9-DXzk0Ijyh47YK9dZ9StBF87bEgLOWUQhzztC2taVsTJ4ks_FIsjWjjHt71XmZ-blIyyUWYTv0U3pkQTlesxrNJbnL8VOgNFV1pG6Dmz66b2la "Tradition reigns in one of the richest congressional districts. Or does it?,"] Yahoo, June 4, 2026.</ref><ref name=forward/> While a 14-year-old in high school, he authored the 224-page book ''The Magic Of Micah Lasher: More Than Fifty Tricks That Will Amaze & Delight Everyone Including You'' (1996).<ref name=forward/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Lasher |first1=Micah |title=The Magic Of Micah Lasher: More Than Fifty Tricks That Will Amaze & Delight Everyone Including You |date=1996-09-01 |publisher=Simon & Schuster Trade |isbn=9780684813905}}</ref><ref name="Micah Lasher, Child Magician">{{cite web |last1=Stein |first1=Joel |title=Micah Lasher, Child Magician |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/04/micah-lasher-child-magician/686989/ |website=The Atlantic |language=en |date=30 April 2026}}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1994/12/07/nyregion/about-new-york-as-magicians-hone-art-presto-woman-appears.html?searchResultPosition=2 "ABOUT NEW YORK; As Magicians Hone Art, Presto, Woman Appears,"] The New York Times, December 7, 1994.</ref>

In 1998 as a 16-year-old student at [[Stuyvesant High School]], he became an editor-in-chief of the school's student newspaper, ''[[The Spectator (Stuyvesant High School)|The Stuyvesant Spectator]]''.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/17/nyregion/student-journalists-without-newspaper-school-halts-publication-raising-question.html?searchResultPosition=3 "Student Journalists Without a Newspaper; School Halts Publication, Raising Question of First Amendment Rights,"] The New York Times, April 17, 1998.</ref> In 1999, after the school's assistant principal pleaded guilty to sexually abusing a 15-year-old female student, Lasher condemned the fact that the assistant principal was only sentenced to three years' probation and was receiving a full pension.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1999/08/18/nyregion/probation-for-teacher-guilty-of-abuse-at-stuyvesant.html?searchResultPosition=7 "Probation For Teacher Guilty of Abuse At Stuyvesant,"] The New York Times, August 18, 1999.,</ref> Lasher graduated from Stuyvesant High School in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lifton |first=Eli Smith, Noa Salas Adam, Evelyn |title=Micah Lasher Reflects on His Time at Stuyvesant |url=https://stuyspec.com/article/micah-lasher-reflects-on-his-time-at-stuyvesant |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=stuyspec.com |language=en}}</ref>

He graduated from [[New York University]] in 2003 with a degree in [[sociology]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Lasher |first=Micah |title=LinkedIn Page of Micah Lasher |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/micah-lasher/ |access-date=March 9, 2025 |website=LinkedIn}}</ref> While at NYU, Lasher spent a semester in London, where he was roommates with [[Aziz Ansari]].<ref name="Micah Lasher, Child Magician"/> Before he graduated from college, he was a founding partner of the national political consulting firm [[SKDKnickerbocker]] (now called [[SKDK]]), advising elected government officials, labor unions, and nonprofits.<ref name=yahoo/><ref name=found/><ref name=announce/> ''The New York Times'' reported that he "has been called a political whiz kid ever since he helped to found an influential political consulting firm while still in college."<ref name=out/>

== Political career ==
===Early years===
Lasher's first job, when he was 16 years old and a junior in high school, was as deputy campaign manager for  [[Eric Schneiderman]]'s winning campaign for the [[New York State Senate]] in 1998.<ref>[https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/meet-voters-new-yorks-12th-congressional-district/414132/ "Meet the voters of New York’s 12th Congressional District,"] cityandstateny, June 15. 2026.</ref><ref name=first/><ref name=announce/> When he was 17 years old, he was an informal adviser to New York State Assemblyman [[Scott Stringer]].<ref name=announce/> In 2001, when Lasher was 19, he managed [[Brad Hoylman-Sigal]]'s campaign for [[New York City Council]] out of his dorm room.<ref name=":2" /><ref>[https://citylimits.org/metropolitan-operatives/ "Metropolitan Operatives,"] City Limits, March 1, 2001.</ref> From 2007 to 2009, he worked as a special assistant and  chief aide to [[Jerrold Nadler]].<ref name=forward>[https://forward.com/news/766762/micah-lasher-jerry-nadler-congress/ "From Jewish teen magician to congressional contender: Meet Micah Lasher, Jerry Nadler’s heir apparent,"] The Forward, September 4, 2025.</ref><ref name=found>[https://www.chalkbeat.org/newyork/2010/1/21/21093974/magical-wunderkind-lobbyist-micah-lasher-gets-promoted/ "Magical wunderkind lobbyist Micah Lasher gets promoted,"] Chalkbeat, January 21, 2010.</ref>

In 2009, he was the Executive Director of Public Affairs and a lobbyist for the [[New York City Department of Education]], as well as a trustee of the [[Community Service Society of New York]], an antipoverty organization.<ref name=marry/>

===NYC Director of State Legislative Affairs===
From 2010 to 2012, Lasher was Director of State Legislative Affairs, the city's chief lobbyist,  for [[New York City Mayor]] [[Michael Bloomberg]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2011/12/08/nyregion/bill-on-hailing-livery-cabs-is-delayed.html?searchResultPosition=19 "Livery Cab Proposal Faces New Uncertainty,"] The New York Times, December 7, 2011.</ref><ref name=out>[https://archive.nytimes.com/cityroom.blogs.nytimes.com/2010/02/17/out-with-the-old-commisioners-in-with-the-new/?searchResultPosition=13 "Out With the Old Commissioners, In With the New,"] The New York Times, February 17, 2010.</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> During his time in that role, he criticized proposed state budget cuts to the city’s [[senior centers]], which he called "an unusually painful and disproportionate cut to a very vulnerable population," supported a  new law under which hundreds of former New York City factory buildings and warehouses were able to become legal [[residential loft]]s, and took part in negotiating an agreement creating a new [[Teacher quality assessment|teacher evaluation system]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/08/nyregion/08seniors.html?searchResultPosition=14 "Obscure Budget Proposal Threatens Senior Centers,"] The New York Times, March 7, 2010.</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2010/07/26/nyregion/26loft.html?searchResultPosition=15 "That Cheap, Roomy Loft Can Now Be a Legal One, Too,"] The New York Times, July 25, 2010.</ref><ref name=teach>[https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/04/nyregion/group-aims-to-counter-influence-of-teachers-union.html?searchResultPosition=21 "Group Aims to Counter Influence of Teachers’ Union in New York,"] The New York Times, April 3, 2010.</ref>

===Executive Director of StudentsFirstNY===
In 2012, he became the Executive Director of [[StudentsFirst| StudentsFirstNY]], the New York branch of  a national education reform advocacy organization founded to promote the expansion of [[charter school]]s and the firing of ineffective teachers, and to oppose [[tenure]].<ref name=teach/> In response to criticism from liberal advocacy groups and labor unions, Lasher said that his group was "a union for students, fighting for a quality teacher for every child," and that the interests of the teachers' union were not always aligned with the interests of  schoolchildren.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/18/nyregion/new-coalition-will-challenge-bloombergs-education-policies.html?searchResultPosition=22 "New Coalition to Challenge Bloomberg’s Education Policies,"] The New York Times, May 17, 2012.</ref>

===Chief of Staff of NY State Attorney General===
In 2013, [[New York State Attorney General]] [[Eric Schneiderman]] hired Lasher as Chief of Staff, a position in which he managed 1,800 people.<ref name=alpha/><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Parsnow |first=Luke |date=January 11, 2024 |title=Micah Lasher leaves post as Hochul's director of policy |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2024/01/11/micah-lasher-leaves-post-as-hochul-s-director-of-policy |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=[[Spectrum News 1 Central New York]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=first>[https://www.nytimes.com/2013/03/26/nyregion/attorney-general-picks-micah-lasher-to-be-chief-of-staff.html?searchResultPosition=27 "Attorney General Picks Ex-Bloomberg Aide to Be Chief of Staff,"] The New York Times, March 25, 2013.</ref> In that role, he  he helped coordinate a lawsuit against Donald Trump and [[Trump University]].<ref name=trumpu/> Lasher also served as an aide and community liaison for [[U.S. Representative|Congressman]] [[Jerrold Nadler]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

=== New York Senate campaign ===
In [[2016 New York State Senate election|2016]], Lasher ran for the [[New York Senate]] in the [[New York's 31st State Senate district|31st district]], in the northern and western edge of Manhattan, after [[Adriano Espaillat]] left the position to successfully run for the [[U.S. House of Representatives]].<ref name=end/> He was endorsed by ''The New York Times''.<ref name=end>[https://www.nytimes.com/2016/09/03/opinion/endorsements-in-new-york-primary-races.html?searchResultPosition=31 "Endorsements in New York Primary Races,"] The New York Times, September 2, 2016.</ref> Lasher lost to [[Marisol Alcantara]] in the Democratic primary election, as she received a plurality of 32.7% of the vote, and Lasher received 31.6% of the vote–294 votes shy of her total.<ref name=cauc/> She went on to join the [[Independent Democratic Conference]], a caucus of Democrats who formed a power-sharing arrangement with the Senate Republican Conference.<ref name=cauc>{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/politics/alcantara-primary-win-major-victory-senate-idc-article-1.2792739|title=Alcantara's primary win a major victory for Senate IDC|website=[[New York Daily News]]|date=September 14, 2016 |access-date=September 3, 2025|last=}}</ref>

=== Sidewalk Labs ===
From 2017 to 2020, Lasher worked as Head of Policy and Communications at [[Sidewalk Labs]], an [[Alphabet Inc|Alphabet]] Google company the goal of which was to innovate technology and [[urban design]] to improve cities.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=alpha>[https://empirereportnewyork.com/governor-hochul-announces-new-administration-appointments/ "Governor Hochul Announces New Administration Appointments,"] Empire Report, November 22, 2021.</ref> Sidewalk's primary proposed  project, [[Sidewalk Toronto]], was  intended to be an innovative reinvention of Toronto's neglected eastern downtown waterfront, and Sidewalks Labs said it did not intend to own the data it gathered in public spaces and instead would  relinquish control of  the data to an independent organization to be established and named the Civic Data Trust.<ref>[https://www.ctvnews.ca/business/article/sidewalk-labs-to-weigh-suggestions-from-panel-for-toronto-smart-city-project/ "Sidewalk Labs to weigh suggestions from panel for Toronto smart city project,"] The Canadian Press, November 9, 2018</ref> The proposed project generated controversy in Toronto over data privacy and surveillance and was eventually cancelled by Alphabet which cited economic concerns caused by the uncertainty of the economy experiencing the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Toronto|COVID-19 pandemic]] .<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fussell |first1=Sidney |title=The City of the Future Is a Data-Collection Machine |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2018/11/google-sidewalk-labs/575551/ |work=The Atlantic |date=21 November 2018 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Barth |first1=Brian |title=The fight against Google's smart city |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/theworldpost/wp/2018/08/08/sidewalk-labs/ |work=The Washington Post |date=8 August 2018}}</ref>

===Director of Policy of New York State===
In November 2021, [[New York State Governor]] [[Kathy Hochul]] appointed Lasher as Director of Policy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2021 |title=Governor Hochul Announces New Administration Appointments |url=https://www.governor.ny.gov/news/governor-hochul-announces-new-administration-appointments |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=www.governor.ny.gov |language=en}}</ref> During his tenure, Lasher participated in shaping and implementing state policy following Hochul’s ascension to the governorship after Andrew Cuomo's resignation.  In his role, Lasher helped write a set of [[gun law]]s directly after the [[2022 Buffalo shooting]].<ref name=trumpu/>  He resigned from this role in early 2024 to pursue a campaign for the New York State Assembly.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

As of 2024, Lasher had served as the chair of the [[Riverside Park (Manhattan)|Riverside Park]] Conservancy, a non-profit organization supporting the maintenance and improvement of Riverside Park.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":1" />

=== New York State Assembly ===
During the [[2024 New York State Assembly election]], Lasher ran for the [[New York's 69th State Assembly district|69th district]], comprising [[Manhattan Valley]], [[Morningside Heights]], and portions of the [[Upper West Side]] and [[West Harlem, Manhattan|West Harlem]].<ref name=":2" />  He ran in a crowded five-candidate [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary, securing victory with 53% of the vote, 19 per cent ahead of his closest competitor.<ref name=":2" />

Lasher's campaign focused on addressing [[Affordable housing|housing affordability]], advocating for comprehensive [[public education]] reforms, and fostering [[Equality (economics)|economic equality]]. He also proposed solutions for addressing zoning and vacant [[storefront]] issues in his district. Lasher received endorsements from local elected officials and organizations, including U.S. representatives [[Jerry Nadler|Jerrold Nadler]] and [[Adriano Espaillat]], and Manhattan Borough president [[Mark Levine (New York politician)|Mark Levine]].<ref>[https://patch.com/new-york/upper-west-side-nyc/race-eli-northrup-post-big-fundraising-haul-uws-seat "The Race Is On: Eli Northrup Post Big Fundraising Haul For UWS Seat,"] Patch, March 15, 2024.</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> He ran unopposed in the November general election.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Silva |first=Manuela |title=Micah Lasher wins primary for State Assembly District 69 |url=https://www.columbiaspectator.com/city-news/2024/06/26/micah-lasher-wins-primary-for-state-assembly-district-69/ |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=Columbia Daily Spectator}}</ref>

In April 2025, Lasher co-sponsored a bill requiring an audit of a state subsidy agreement with [[Elon Musk]]'s [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] in order to "identify waste, fraud and abuse committed by private parties to the contract."<ref name=tesla/> It would assess whether Tesla is meeting job creation targets, making promised investments, paying sufficient rent, and meeting job training commitments.<ref name=tesla/> If Tesla were not in compliance, the state could claw back state benefits,assess  penalties, and  end contracts.<ref name=tesla/> Lasher said: "It is the height of hypocrisy that Elon Musk, the man who is dismantling federal agencies and doing enormous damage on the basis of wildly unsubstantiated claims of waste, fraud and abuse, is the beneficiary of one of the biggest, shadiest subsidy deals of all time,"<ref name=tesla>[https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/02/nyregion/trump-musk-ny-tesla.html?searchResultPosition=51 "N.Y. Lawmakers Fight Trump With a Proposal Targeting Elon Musk,"] The New York Times, April 2, 2025.</ref>

Also in April 2025, he worked to rescue the [[Metro Theater (New York City)|Metro Theater]], a [[New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission|landmark]] 1933 [[Art Deco]] movie theater on [[Broadway (Manhattan)|Broadway]] near West 99th Street on the Upper West Side.<ref name=hoch/> The movie theater received discretionary grants from New York Governor Kathy Hochul, whom he had lobbied, as well as from the New York State Senate.<ref name=hoch>[https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/06/movies/metro-theater-sold-hochul-grants.html?searchResultPosition=61 "Upper West Side Theater Is Sold After Governor Allocates $3.5 Million,"] The New York Times, April 6, 2025.</ref>

In June 2025, amid concern [[President Trump]] might seek to strip federal laws governing [[housing discrimination]], a New York State  bill that he co-sponsored was adopted by New York State lawmakers.<ref name=housing/> The intent of the bill was to pre-empt any such potential rollback by allowing prosecutors to bring [[housing discrimination]] cases based on conditions in residences,  rather than them being required to prove intent to discriminate.<ref name=housing/> Lasher said: "It would mean that the state law is no longer weaker than the federal law, and clarify any question now or in the future about whether claims brought under state law must meet some higher burden."<ref name=housing>[https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/19/nyregion/new-york-legislature-ai-prison-reform.html?searchResultPosition=47 "N.Y. Lawmakers Target Prison Reform and A.I. in Frantic End of Session,"], The New York Times, June 20, 2025.</ref>

In November 2025, in the wake of a rowdy and chaotic protest  at the entryway of [[Park East Synagogue]], which included chants of "[[Death, death to the IDF|Death to the IDF]]" and "[[Globalize the intifada]]," and an exhortation that "We need to make them scared!," Lasher said: "If you are standing outside a [[synagogue]] calling for 'intifada revolution,' you are not peacefully protesting. You are trying to intimidate and create fear among Jews, and that is never acceptable."<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/24/nyregion/mamdani-synagogue-protest.html?searchResultPosition=33 "Mamdani Response to Protest Inflames Tensions With Jewish Leaders,"] The New York Times, November 24, 2025.</ref>

In December 2025, in the wake of [[Deportation in the second Trump administration|President Trump's "mass deportations]]", Lasher cosponsored legislation to designate  schools, houses of worship, and nonprofit offices as off-limits to federal agents trying to make [[administrative arrest]]s or arrests without a  judicial [[arrest warrant]]. That way, he said, "our neighbors can function freely in our communities and deal with the basic needs of life, and do so not in the shadows."<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/18/us/politics/democrats-trump-deportations.html?searchResultPosition=32 "Democratic State Lawmakers Vow to Unite and Push Back on Trump’s Deportations ,"] The New York Times, December 18, 2025.</ref>

{{main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New York#District 12}}

In September 2025, U.S. Representative [[Jerry Nadler]] announced that he would retire from his congressional seat when his then-current term ended; it was reported that Nadler planned on supporting Lasher in a prospective primary.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Fandos |first=Nicholas |date=September 1, 2025 |title=Nadler, Pillar of Democratic Party's Old Guard, Will Retire Next Year |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/01/nyregion/jerrold-nadler-congress-retires.html |access-date=2025-09-01 |website=[[New York Times]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Fandos |first=Nicholas |date=September 2, 2025 |title=A Kennedy, a Protégé and a Progressive Star Eye Nadler's N.Y. House Seat |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/02/nyregion/nadler-retire-successor-replace.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share&referringSource=articleShare |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=[[New York Times]] |language=en}}</ref> On September 15, Lasher decided to run for Nadler's seat.<ref name=announce>{{Cite web |last=Ashford |first=Grace |date=September 15, 2025 |title=Lasher, Nadler's Protégé, Says He Is Running to Succeed His Mentor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/15/nyregion/nyc-micah-lasher-jerrold-nadler.html |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=[[New York Times]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Barkan |first=Ross |date=September 15, 2025 |url=https://www.crainsnewyork.com/politics/politics-could-micah-lasher-easily-win-race-replace-nadler |title=On Politics: Race to replace Nadler has an early front-runner |work=Crain's New York Business}}</ref> ''The New York Times'' wrote of the district, [[New York's 12th congressional district]]: "Stretching from [[Union Square, Manhattan|Union Square]] through [[Central Park]], the district is home to more [[Fortune 500 companies]], millionaires, and cultural landmarks than perhaps anywhere in the country," is "one of the oldest, best-educated and wealthiest districts in the United States," and that it is  "one of the most Democratic congressional districts in the United States."<ref name=":8"/><ref name=announce/><ref name=wonp/>

Lasher said that his number one priority would be to fight what he has called the [[Trump administration]]'s assault on the [[Constitution of the United States]], democratic norms, and vital public programs.<ref name=announce/> His policy proposals also include raising the [[Minimum wage in the United States|federal minimum wage]], passing [[Medicare for All]], and abolishing [[ICE]], which he said had become "the embodiment of a thugocracy" and a "completely unchecked, almost militia-like, organization."<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/15/us/politics/democrats-abolish-ice-slogan.html?searchResultPosition=29 "Abolish ICE? It’s a Slogan Some Democratic Critics of ICE Would Abolish,"] The New York Times, January 15, 2026.</ref><ref name=announce/> He believes that Democrats in Congress should be willing to shut down the government instead of funding what he calls the Trump administration's "fascist policies."<ref name=announce/> He has also proposed redrawing [[New York's congressional districts|New York's congressional district maps]] in response to [[2025–2026 United States redistricting|redistricting efforts in Republican-led states]], and has proposed legislation in that regard.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/19/nyregion/nadler-candidates-who-running.html?searchResultPosition=34 "Who’s Running to Replace Jerry Nadler? 7 People and Counting.,"] The New York Times, November 19, 2025.</ref> He opposes legislation that would prohibit weapons sales to Israel.<ref name=trumpu>[https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/18/nyregion/micah-lasher-congress-manhattan.html?searchResultPosition=1 "Can a Nerd Still Get Elected to Congress in Manhattan?,"] The New York Times, June 18, 2026.</ref> After [[Zohran Mamdani]] became the nominee of the Democratic Party in his campaign to become mayor of New York City, Lasher supported him, while at the same time writing that he hoped that Mamdani "can come to better appreciate the deeply personal and historical importance that the survival of Israel as a [[Jewish state]] holds for [[Jewish New Yorkers]]. I hope that he is able to see [[antisemitism]] when it takes the form of a [[New antisemitism|double-standard being applied to Israel]] precisely because it is a Jewish state."<ref name=announce/><ref>Micah Lasher. [https://x.com/MicahLasher/status/1939430511094423959 "Post"], Twitter,  June 29, 2025.</ref>

Lasher was endorsed by former New York City mayor [[Michael Bloomberg]], U.S. representatives [[Jerry Nadler]] and [[Nydia Velázquez]], [[Governor of New York]] [[Kathy Hochul]], former Governor of New York [[David Paterson]], and former [[Attorney General of New York]] [[Eric Schneiderman]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lebowitz |first1=Megan |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Rep. Jerry Nadler endorses former aide Micah Lasher to be his successor |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/rep-jerry-nadler-endorses-former-aide-micah-lasher-successor-rcna258146 |access-date=February 9, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]]}}</ref><ref name="EndTrack">{{cite web |last1=Eichholz |first1=Jack |title=2026 Endorsement Tracker |url=https://votehub.com/2026-endorsements |website=VoteHub |access-date=January 16, 2026 |language=en |date=January 8, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Levingston |first1=Miranda |title=Governor Hochul Endorses A Candidate In NY-12's Race |url=https://patch.com/new-york/upper-west-side-nyc/governor-hochul-endorses-candidate-ny-12s-race |website=Patch |access-date=April 13, 2026 |language=en |date=April 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://amsterdamnews.com/news/2026/04/30/im-supporting-micah-lasher-for-congress-heres-why/|title=OP-ED: I'm supporting Micah Lasher for Congress. Here's why.|last=Paterson|first=David|date=April 30, 2026|access-date=May 29, 2026|website=[[New York Amsterdam News]]}}</ref><ref name="CityState6/15">{{cite news |last1=McDonough|first1=Annie|title=Meet the voters of New York's 12th Congressional District |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/06/meet-voters-new-yorks-12th-congressional-district/414132/?oref=csny-homepage-river |website=[[City & State]] |date=June 15, 2026|access-date=June 15, 2026}}</ref><ref name=announce/>

Lasher won the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026, defeating [[Alex Bores]], [[George Conway]], and [[Jack Schlossberg]].<ref name=wonp>[https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/nyregion/ny12-nadler-primary-micah-lasher.html "Micah Lasher Wins Manhattan Primary, Defeating Kennedy Heir and Others,"] The New York Times, June 24, 2026.</ref>

Lasher won New York's 12th Congressional District seat in the general election on November 3, 2026. He defeated Republican nominee [[Caroline Shinkle]] by a margin of at least 143,402 votes, with about 77 percent of the vote to Shinkle’s 20 percent.<ref name="ReynoldsSmithRennisonBlum2026-1" /> Lasher will take his seat in Congress when the new session begins on January 3, 2027.<ref name="www.congress.gov-1">{{Cite web |title=The First Day of a New Congress: A Guide to Proceedings on the House Floor |url=https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/RL30725 |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=www.congress.gov}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Lasher lives on the [[Upper West Side]] of Manhattan with his family.<ref name=":2" /> His wife, whom he married in 2009, is named Elizabeth, and they have three children.<ref name=marry>[https://www.nytimes.com/2009/08/23/fashion/weddings/23MANN.html?searchResultPosition=10 "Elizabeth Mann, Micah Lasher,"] The New York Times, August 21, 2009.</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Meet Micah Lasher |url=https://micahlasher.com/meet-micah-lasher}}</ref> He is Jewish, and his family is a member of  [[Congregation Rodeph Sholom (Manhattan)|Congregation Rodeph Sholom]].<ref name=rod/><ref name="70Faces">{{cite web |last1=Gilson |first1=Grace |title=A betrayal or politics as usual? A state rep's endorsement of Zohran Mamdani roils Orthodox rabbis on the Upper West Side |url=https://www.jta.org/2025/07/03/united-states/a-manhattan-pols-endorsement-of-zohran-mamdani-sparks-a-facebook-fracas |website=JTA |date=3 July 2025 |publisher=70 Faces Media |access-date=2 September 2025}}</ref>
